ports.name: clk_i
ports.functionality: Supplies the rising edge used by all clocked processes; sequences updates to bus response, control registers, counter, reset requests and reset_cause. It times the entity's sequential behaviour.
ports.evidence: rising_edge(clk_i) used in processes bus_access, wdt_counter, reset_generator, reset_identifier

ports.name: rstn_ext_i
ports.functionality: Acts as the asynchronous reset for the reset_identifier process; when asserted low it clears reset_cause to "00" at that process's reset branch.
ports.evidence: process reset_identifier sensitivity (rstn_ext_i) and if (rstn_ext_i = '0') then reset_cause <= "00"

ports.name: rstn_dbg_i
ports.functionality: Is tested at clock edge to select the debug reset cause; when low it causes reset_cause to be set to "01" on the next rising edge.
ports.evidence: if (rstn_dbg_i = '0') then reset_cause <= "01" in reset_identifier process

ports.name: rstn_sys_i
ports.functionality: Provides the asynchronous reset for the main clocked processes; when asserted low it clears bus_rsp_o, ctrl fields, counter state and reset request signals in their reset branches.
ports.evidence: if (rstn_sys_i = '0') then ... in bus_access, wdt_counter, reset_generator processes

ports.name: bus_req_i
ports.functionality: The aggregate record is not referenced as a whole in this source; individual fields of it are read instead (see field annotations).
ports.evidence: Only bus_req_i fields (stb, rw, addr, data, ...) are used in bus_access; no whole-record use

ports.name: bus_req_i.addr
ports.functionality: Its bit 2 is tested to choose between control register writes and password write action; that selection directs which internal registers are updated.
ports.evidence: if (bus_req_i.addr(2) = '0') then ... else ... in bus_access process

ports.name: bus_req_i.data
ports.functionality: Supplies bits and slices for register writes (ctrl fields) and is compared to the reset password; those reads drive control registers and determine reset_wdt/reset_force on writes.
ports.evidence: bus_req_i.data(...) assigned into ctrl fields and compared (bus_req_i.data(31 downto 0) = reset_pwd_c) in bus_access

ports.name: bus_req_i.ben
ports.functionality: Declared bus byte-enable field is not read or used anywhere in this source.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.ben in source

ports.name: bus_req_i.stb
ports.functionality: Gates bus access handling (write/read) and is routed into the response ack field; when asserted it enables the read/write branching in bus_access and also directly becomes bus_rsp_o.ack.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb; if (bus_req_i.stb = '1') then ... in bus_access

ports.name: bus_req_i.rw
ports.functionality: Selects the write versus read branch in bus_access; when '1' the code updates control registers or password action, otherwise it prepares bus response data.
ports.evidence: if (bus_req_i.rw = '1') then ... else ... in bus_access

ports.name: bus_req_i.src
ports.functionality: Declared but not read anywhere in this source.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.src in source

ports.name: bus_req_i.priv
ports.functionality: Declared but not read anywhere in this source.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.priv in source

ports.name: bus_req_i.debug
ports.functionality: Declared but not read anywhere in this source (separate rstn_dbg_i input holds debug reset).
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.debug in source

ports.name: bus_req_i.amo
ports.functionality: Declared but not referenced anywhere in this source.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.amo in source

ports.name: bus_req_i.amoop
ports.functionality: Declared but not referenced anywhere in this source.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.amoop in source

ports.name: bus_req_i.lock
ports.functionality: Declared but not read anywhere in this source; the module has its own ctrl.lock internal field used for locking behaviour.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.lock in source

ports.name: bus_req_i.fence
ports.functionality: Declared but not referenced anywhere in this source.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.fence in source

ports.name: bus_rsp_o
ports.functionality: Drives the bus response bundle to the outside: ack, err and data fields are driven from internal logic and defaults (including reset) to form the module's bus reply.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o <= rsp_terminate_c in reset branch; individual fields assigned in bus_access process

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.ack
ports.functionality: Is set each clock to the incoming strobe (bus_req_i.stb) and thus reports handshake acknowledgment to the bus master.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb in bus_access (rising_edge(clk_i))

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.err
ports.functionality: Is driven low each clock in the bus_access process (constant '0'), providing the error indicator in the response.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.err <= '0' in bus_access process (rising_edge(clk_i))

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.data
ports.functionality: Holds response data; defaulted to zeros each clock and selectively populated from control and reset_cause fields on read operations before being exported on the bus.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.data(...) <= ctrl.* and bus_rsp_o.data <= (others => '0') in bus_access

ports.name: clkgen_en_o
ports.functionality: Mirrors the internal ctrl.enable bit to an external clkgen enable output; directly driven by the control register value.
ports.evidence: clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable (concurrent assignment)

ports.name: clkgen_i
ports.functionality: Provides prescaler ticks by indexing a selected bit; a selected bit of this vector is carried to prsc_tick for internal timing.
ports.evidence: prsc_tick <= clkgen_i(clk_div4096_c) concurrent assignment

ports.name: rstn_o
ports.functionality: Drives the external reset output as the inverted OR of the two hardware reset request signals (hw_rst_timeout and hw_rst_access); reports whether a hardware reset is asserted.
ports.evidence: rstn_o <= not (hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access) concurrent assignment

signals.name: ctrl
signals.functionality: Holds the WDT control fields (enable, lock, strict, timeout) which are individually captured from bus writes and reset; the record groups those fields for internal use.
signals.evidence: type ctrl_t record and individual field assignments in bus_access process

signals.name: ctrl.enable
signals.functionality: Captured from bus write (specific data bit) or cleared on reset; read by the counter and reset logic and forwarded outside as clkgen_en_o and in bus reads.
signals.evidence: ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_enable_c) in bus_access; used in wdt_counter and clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable

signals.name: ctrl.lock
signals.functionality: Captured from bus write (combined with current enable) and read back; it gates whether subsequent writes to control fields are allowed and thus prevents modifications when set.
signals.evidence: ctrl.lock <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_lock_c) and ctrl.enable in bus_access; used to decide write acceptance

signals.name: ctrl.strict
signals.functionality: Captured from a bus write and read back; when set it allows bus-induced accesses to request a hardware reset (used in hw_rst_access generation).
signals.evidence: ctrl.strict <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_strict_c) in bus_access; used in hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force

signals.name: ctrl.timeout
signals.functionality: Captured from a slice of the bus write data and held; compared to the running counter to detect timeout and exported in bus reads.
signals.evidence: ctrl.timeout <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_timeout_msb_c downto ctrl_timeout_lsb_c) and used in (cnt = ctrl.timeout)

signals.name: prsc_tick
signals.functionality: Carries a selected bit of clkgen_i into the internal tick signal and supplies timing to the counter logic and reset generator.
signals.evidence: prsc_tick <= clkgen_i(clk_div4096_c); prsc_tick used in wdt_counter and reset_generator

signals.name: cnt
signals.functionality: Holds the running counter value; increments when cnt_inc is true, is cleared on disable or reset_wdt, and is compared against ctrl.timeout to detect timeout.
signals.evidence: cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1) in wdt_counter; comparison (cnt = ctrl.timeout) used in cnt_timeout

signals.name: cnt_started
signals.functionality: Captured from the conjunction of ctrl.enable and prescaler activity (or prior started state); it records whether counting is active and is used in increment qualification and timeout logic.
signals.evidence: cnt_started <= ctrl.enable and (cnt_started or prsc_tick) in wdt_counter; cnt_started used in cnt_timeout and cnt_inc

signals.name: cnt_inc
signals.functionality: Captured each clock as the AND of prsc_tick and cnt_started; when high it gates the counter increment in the next step.
signals.evidence: cnt_inc <= prsc_tick and cnt_started in wdt_counter; used in if (cnt_inc = '1') then cnt <= cnt + 1

signals.name: cnt_timeout
signals.functionality: Combinationally asserted when counting has started and the counter equals the configured timeout; this signal is then used to request a hardware timeout reset.

signals.name: reset_cause
signals.functionality: Holds a two-bit code indicating why the last reset occurred; updated by debug, timeout or access reset conditions and read-out on bus reads.
signals.evidence: reset_cause set in reset_identifier process on rstn_dbg_i, hw_rst_timeout, hw_rst_access; read into bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_rcause_hi_c downto ctrl_rcause_lo_c)

signals.name: hw_rst_timeout
signals.functionality: Captured from ctrl.enable, cnt_timeout and prsc_tick; when asserted it contributes to the reset output and selects the timeout reset cause.
signals.evidence: hw_rst_timeout <= ctrl.enable and cnt_timeout and prsc_tick in reset_generator; used in rstn_o and reset_identifier

signals.name: hw_rst_access
signals.functionality: Captured from ctrl.enable, ctrl.strict and reset_force; when asserted it contributes to the reset output and selects the access reset cause.
signals.evidence: hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force in reset_generator; used in rstn_o and reset_identifier

signals.name: reset_wdt
signals.functionality: Captured when a write with the correct reset password occurs; when asserted it clears the counter on the next cycle (used to reset the watchdog timer).
signals.evidence: reset_wdt <= '1' when bus_req_i.data(31 downto 0) = reset_pwd_c in bus_access; wdt_counter checks (reset_wdt = '1') to clear cnt

signals.name: reset_force
signals.functionality: Set when invalid register access or unauthorized write attempts occur (locked writes or wrong password); used as input to hw_rst_access generation.
signals.evidence: reset_force <= '1' in bus_access when writes are invalid; used in hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force
